name: Microsoft Fairwater AI datacenter, Mount Pleasant
summary: Microsoft AI supercomputing campus in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, on land originally slated for Foxconn. The first facility (Phase 1, near County Road KR and 90th Street) has three buildings with about 1.2 million sq ft on 315 acres; equipment came online in April 2026 and Microsoft declared it fully operational on 23 June 2026. A second facility of similar scale (Phase 2), immediately adjacent near KR and County Road H, has been under construction since November 2025 with completion scheduled for 2028. Microsoft pledged USD 3.3 billion for the first facility and USD 4 billion more for the second, and calls the site Fairwater.

location.note: Microsoft's construction page headings place Phase 1 at 'KR & 90' and Phase 2 at 'KR & H' (County Road KR with 90th Street and County Road H); Spectrum News says the site was originally slated for Foxconn. Coordinates are the OpenStreetMap feature named Microsoft Fairwater AI Datacenter (via Nominatim); OSM maps Phase 2 slightly further west at about 42.6780, -87.9076.

parties.note: Microsoft reports about 550 full-time employees on site at the completed first facility.

parties.name: Walsh Construction
parties.note: Named on Microsoft's construction update page for foundation work from November 2023 and as the Phase 2 contractor from November 2025.

parties.name: Kiewit
parties.note: Named on Microsoft's construction update page in September and October 2024 as a main contractor working along County Road KR and County Road H.

parties.name: We Energies
parties.note: Microsoft cites a partnership with We Energies, and its February 2024 construction update said We Energies would soon start building a substation on the western part of the parcel.

parties.name: National Grid Renewables
parties.note: Partner on a 250 MW Wisconsin solar project announced alongside the campus; a renewable matching arrangement rather than a stated direct feed to the site.

parties.name: NVIDIA
parties.note: Microsoft describes the cluster as built on NVIDIA GB200 servers with Blackwell GPUs.

parties.name: OpenAI
parties.note: Reported, not confirmed: Microsoft says its AI datacenters power OpenAI, and Epoch AI lists OpenAI as a likely user of this site.

metrics.note: Announced in May 2024 for spending through the end of 2026; Microsoft later called it the initial investment pledge, with the second datacenter funded separately.
Additional spend over three years on a second datacenter of similar size and scale.

Epoch AI modeled estimate of current IT power (timeline entries of April and May 2026), not a company figure. Microsoft has not published a megawatt figure for the site.

milestones.note: Epoch AI dates the start of land clearing to 14 July 2023; Microsoft's update page reported permits received and grading planned from July 2023, with Walsh starting foundation work in November 2023.
The Associated Press reported that in late December 2024 Microsoft disclosed it was pausing later phases of a large Wisconsin datacenter project.
Second datacenter of similar size announced with an additional USD 4 billion.
Start of Phase 2 work by Walsh Construction at KR and County Road H.

Microsoft says equipment came online with startup activities in April 2026; Epoch AI lists Building 1 as operational on 16 April 2026. Microsoft declared the first facility fully operational on 2026-06-23.
Scheduled completion of the second facility (Phase 2); Microsoft's construction page says early 2028.

power_sources.description: Grid supply via We Energies; Microsoft said in February 2024 that We Energies would soon start a substation on the western part of the parcel.
Microsoft is matching the site with renewable contracts, including a 250 MW solar project in Portage County, Wisconsin, developed with National Grid Renewables and expected to operate in 2027.
